title: Implantation of a Pelvic Nerve Array in Rats
author: James B Fallon
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bfwxjpfn
materials: Administer analgesic and sterile Hartmann’s solution.

steps.title: Sterilize nerve arrays
steps.instruction: Sterilise the pelvic nerve arrays by sonication followed by autoclaving. Perform sonication cycles of 15 min in 5 % Pyroneg, then 5 min in distilled water, another 5 min in distilled water, 10 min in 96 % ethanol, followed by two further 5 min washes in distilled water, and finally autoclave the arrays.

steps.title: Anesthetise and prepare animal
steps.instruction: Induce anaesthesia in an adult male Sprague‑Dawley rat (8–10 weeks old) with 2.5 % isoflurane in oxygen (adjust as required for maintenance). Apply eye lubricant and place the animal on a heated pad.

steps.title: Shave and disinfect surgical sites
steps.instruction: Shave the ventral abdomen and the dorsal‑lumbar back, then clean both areas with betadine.

steps.title: Create dorsal‑lumbar incision
steps.instruction: Make an incision on the dorsal‑lumbar aspect of the back; this will serve as the exit site for the percutaneous electrode connector.

steps.title: Create ventral midline skin incision
steps.instruction: Make a ventral midline incision in the skin overlying the bladder region.

steps.title: Tunnel array subcutaneously
steps.instruction: Using hemostats, tunnel the sterilised array subcutaneously from the dorsal incision site to the ventral incision site.

steps.title: Expose bladder cavity
steps.instruction: Make an incision in the ventral midline of the abdominal cavity to expose the bladder.

steps.title: Create secondary lateral muscle incision
steps.instruction: Make a second, small (1 cm) incision lateral to the midline incision into the abdominal muscle on the same side as the lead wire, and feed the array through this secondary incision.

steps.title: Expose pelvic ganglia
steps.instruction: Locate the left or right prostate, gently retract the lobe to reveal the pelvic ganglia and connecting nerves, including the pelvic nerve.

steps.title: Secure array to pelvic nerve
steps.instruction: Place the array over the top of the pelvic nerve and secure it to the connective tissue of the prostate using 7‑0 silk sutures.

steps.title: Exteriorise lead wire
steps.instruction: Exteriorise the lead wire through the abdominal cavity via the second small incision.

steps.title: Close abdominal and skin incisions
steps.instruction: Close the abdominal cavity and all skin incision sites with appropriate sutures.

steps.title: Secure percutaneous pedestal
steps.instruction: Suture the percutaneous pedestal (silicone‑Dacron embedded mesh) to the underlying muscle and connective tissue of the dorsal midline near the neck using 2‑0 silk.

steps.title: Close dorsal skin incision
steps.instruction: Close the dorsal skin incision site with sutures.

steps.title: Post‑operative plug care
steps.instruction: During post‑surgery management, clean the skin around the percutaneous plug with betadine every 2 weeks to prevent infection; rats may be awake but should be gently restrained during this procedure.

steps.title: Optional bladder catheter implantation
steps.instruction: At this stage, a bladder catheter can be implanted according to the protocol described in “Cystometry for Awake Rats” (Janet R. Keast).
